H1.title: Attack effectiveness
H1.statement: Full suppression of a single modality significantly reduces fixed-fusion macro-F1.
H1.test: one-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank (clean > attacked) per modality, Holm-corrected

H2.title: Modality sensitivity
H2.statement: Modalities differ in their vulnerability to targeted suppression.
H2.test: Friedman test on per-subject macro-F1 drops across modalities (Kendall's W), Holm post-hoc

H3.title: Mitigation without material clean loss
H3.statement: Reliability-aware fusion improves macro-F1 over fixed fusion under the same attack, while its clean macro-F1 loss stays within the non-inferiority margin (0.02).
H3.test: one-sided paired Wilcoxon (defended > fixed) per modality, Holm-corrected; bootstrap non-inferiority

H4.title: Detectability of suppression
H4.statement: Suppression produces a reliability signature that separates attacked from clean windows (AUROC > 0.5) at a clean false-rejection rate no higher than 0.1.
H4.test: one-sided one-sample Wilcoxon of per-subject AUROC against 0.5, Holm-corrected; bootstrap FRR

targeted_vs_random.statement: Strategically chosen suppression degrades fixed fusion more than random modality loss.
